ambient_trade.text: Wool is fetching {gold} a bale in {town} this week. Anyone with salt to trade, shout befor the caravans fill up.
Salt out of {town} is up again. If you're hauling south, I'll pay good coin for the empty space in your carts.
Spare draft horses going for {gold} each, sound legs and calm temper. Name your offer, I'm listening.
Good salt price in {town} today, though the toll-keeper takes his cut before you see a single crown back.
Buying fleeces by the bundle, paid in silver on delivery. Lowest price goes to whoever stops shouting and starts counting.

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I don't trust you and you don't trust me, but {gold} for the cart is a number we can both live with.
Ser {player}, I still have a long list of complaints about you, but {gold} for the wool in {town} is a fair figure. I'll sign.
Ser {player}, {gold} for the salt delivered to {town}. A fair price for both of us, and nobody has to draw steel on the road.
{player}, you always know how to make my day. {gold} it is, and I'll throw in a spare saddle for the trip to {town}.
Deal, {player}. Shake on it, and next caravan I'll put your name on the first cart out of {town}.

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. Our carts run the same road, so let's trade words before anyone gets nervous.
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here, hauling wool and salt. Got any coin you'd rather trade than spend on a fight?
Ser {player}! Good to see a friendly face on this road. Are you buying, or just passing through with that fine horse?
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I won't pretend we're friends, but I'll sell you salt at a fair price if your swords stay sheathed.
Keep your hands off the cart, {player}. Talk prices first, because a burned cart earns nothing for either of us.

player_raided_my_village.text: Burning {village} was bad for business, {player}. Every barn you torched is money nobody here will spend on your roads.
{player}, {village} is still smoking and my wool is stuck in the mud. Pay for the damage and I'll still talk terms.
Word is {village} got hit. Tolls and raids both eat into profit, and I'm not happy about either.
Ser {player}, you owe {village} more than an apology. Send silver to the folk you burned and we can start again.
{village} lost its stores and nobody is getting a discount for it. Settle up with the folk there, {player}, then we'll talk.

war_declared.text: War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Good luck to the armies, but every closed road means half my carts sit in the yard.
{my_faction} has declared on {enemy_faction}. Wool prices will jump by week's end, so anyone holding stock, sell now.
Blades out between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Ledgers will be a mess for months, so write when roads reopen.
I'm parking my carts until someone pays me to move them. Wars are good for swords and bad for everything else.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. Carts can roll again, and I've already got three orders waiting.
{my_faction} signed terms with {faction}. Bring out the salt, the tolls are about to get a lot friendlier.
Finally, {faction} and {my_faction} stopped swinging. Old quarrels aside, I'd rather haggle over prices than over bodies.
Good news for trade routes. Fewer ambushes means more wool on the road and prices that finally settle.

released_by_player.text: Released by {player} with no ransom asked. That's the kind of deal I like. Drinks are on me next time we meet.
Ser {player}, I won't forget this. Ransom waived, and I'll set a proper deal for the salt routes next time.
Freed by {player} without ransom. Fair enough, though next time I expect a receipt for the trouble.
{player}, letting me go for free was generous. I'll still send you a discount letter, and you'll get it on time.
Free again, thanks to {player}. Don't mistake it for forgiveness. I keep a ledger of every debt, and yours is still open.

beat_by_player.text: Lost the field to {player} with {troop_count} men down. Bad luck and bad for business, but I'll be back with better prices.
{player}, you beat my {troop_count} men fair and square. Shall we talk about the losses before the carts get stuck?
{player}, that field cost me {troop_count} men and a wagon of salt. I'm still angry, but I'll hear your terms if they're fair.
Ser {player}, you caught us with {troop_count} troops and I'll admit it was well played. What would it take to end this without more losses?

whisper_beg_help.text: Ser {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing {fief} and my coffers are thin. Send men and I'll pay well, name your price.
Ser {player}, I hate to beg, but {fief} is losing ground to {enemy_faction}. Name a price and it's yours.
My friend {player}, {fief} needs you more than my ledger does. Hold it for me and I'll cover your upkeep.
{player}, {enemy_faction} is at {fief}'s gates. I can't hold this alone. Send your sword and I'll pay by the day.

ambient_complaint.text: Bandits hit the road again outside {town}. Another wool cart lost, and the guard fees I pay are robbery in their own right.
{rival} is undercutting the whole market with cheap salt. Either they're smuggling or they've got friends at the toll house.
Tolls on the {faction} roads are up again. Every merchant in the valley is paying for someone else's war.
{rival} got my last shipment rerouted and now wants me to pay for the detour. Grudge noted, and so is the invoice.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain turned the road outside {town} into soup, and I'm still paying for the wagon wheels.
Anyone know if {village} is still trading in candles? I'm low on stock and the prices there are a mystery.
Lag on this server is worse than the bandits. My ledger keeps freezing mid-sale.
Quiet week for the shipping lanes. Fine by me, the bandits are on holiday and the prices are settling.
Market at {village} is busy again, and somebody is finally selling decent rope. Mind your purses out there.
